function: Excluded, above_phy (p. 5): the DRL agent allocates uplink bandwidth, downlink bandwidth, and MEC computing resources to queued sensing-data fusion tasks to maximize task completion rate.
notes: The title on p. 1 matches the DOI. Exclusion code above_phy. The learned method is a TD3-style DRL agent (double critics, delayed actor update, target networks). Its actions are 'uplink bandwidth aui(t), MEC server computing resource aci(t), and downlink bandwidth adi(t)' (p. 5) for the tasks in the execution queue. The goal is to 'improve the completion rate of collaborative sensing tasks by reasonably allocating limited wireless communication and edge computing resources in each time slot' (p. 5, problem P1; p. 1: 'joint optimization of wireless and edge computing resources'). This is MEC edge computing resource allocation plus per-task bandwidth scheduling, which the instructions place above the physical layer. Moving tasks between the waiting and execution queues is a fixed priority rule, not learned (p. 7, Algorithm 1). No physical-layer decision is learned jointly. Transmit powers are fixed at 27 and 30 dBm (p. 8). No antennas, beams, waveforms, or RIS appear in the system model: the channel is a scalar gain hi(t) (p. 4) with 3GPP TR 38.901 RMa path loss only (p. 8). The paper says it studies 'the fusion of the functional level' rather than the 'signal fusion model, which focuses on physical layer optimization' (p. 2). Sensing is outside the learned decision: radar sensing and communication use fixed TDMA slots ('There is no interference between all communication and sensing waves due to TDMA', p. 4), and 'this work does not consider the process of collecting sensing data' (p. 3). So no resource that serves both sensing and communication (area 5) is allocated. The metrics are reward, task completion rate, and training time (pp. 9-10). If the reviewer counts bandwidth allocation as physical layer, the work still fails 'function': terrestrial bandwidth and computing allocation is none of the seven areas, and this is not a satellite or aerial link.
